definitions.explanation: Doing something by one's own hand or action.
Acting without being forced or asked.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}が{自|みずか}ら{説明|せつめい}した。
{自|みずか}ら{進|すす}んで{手伝|てつだ}った。
{問題|もんだい}は{自|みずか}らの{行動|こうどう}で{解決|かいけつ}するべきだ。
examples.english: You should solve the problem through your own actions.

notes:
{自|みずか}ら functions as both an adverb (personally, voluntarily) and a pronoun (oneself).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {自|みずか}ら{進|すす}んで (voluntarily, proactively)
- {自|みずか}らの{手|て}で (with one's own hands)
- {自|みずか}らの{意思|いし}で (of one's own will)
- {自|みずか}ら{行動|こうどう}する (to act personally)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {自|みずか}ら vs. {自分|じぶん}: {自分|じぶん} is the common everyday word for "oneself"; {自|みずか}ら emphasizes personal initiative or action and is more formal/literary.
- {自|みずか}ら vs. {自|みずか}らの: {自|みずか}らの functions as a possessive ("one's own").

GRAMMAR NOTE:
When used as a pronoun, {自|みずか}ら takes the possessive particle の: {自|みずか}らの{責任|せきにん} (one's own responsibility).

Register: Formal/literary. More common in written Japanese and formal speech. {自分|じぶん}で is the casual equivalent.
